interpretations.text: Observation — In the finite-budget native MuJoCo search over 0.0–0.6 s, with 31 samples, six tendon-tension channels bounded to 0–8 N, and 18 active control coefficients, the baseline sequence had terminal position error 0.11953014442617846 m, holding maximum position error 0.11953014442617846 m, holding maximum speed 0.34961372144211234 m/s, and signed maximum excess 10.953014442617846. The best-found sequence instead had terminal position error 0.003452366584264502 m, holding maximum position error 0.004096331370682971 m, holding maximum speed 0.028321836968032563 m/s, and signed maximum excess −0.05593876773224782. Its worst sampled constraint was holding speed at 0.5400000000000004 s: 0.028321836968032563 m/s against a 0.03 m/s limit. Thus all represented sampled proxies had nonpositive normalized excess for this best sequence. This is new diagnostic model information, not observed task acceptance.

Hypotheses — H1 is that time-varying tension control within the modeled 0–8 N bounds supplies sufficient authority for the represented task proxies; the transition from the failed baseline to the best sampled sequence supports this locally. H1 predicts comparable constraint margins under an independent full replay from the frozen initial state. H2 is that the apparent margin depends on finite-search, sampling, initialization, or native-model details rather than transferable task capability; it predicts degraded or failed margins under independent replay or frozen acceptance. Neither hypothesis identifies a structural cause: only one start was used, global optimality was not established, some best inputs reached the lower physical bound, and no saved mechanism result is bound to the best-control trajectory. These coupled control differences therefore cannot isolate a tendon, parameter, or failure mechanism.

Discriminating Evidence — Missing evidence includes an independent 0-to-0.6 s replay of the saved best schedule, evaluation by the original frozen task-acceptance procedure, and applicable geometry, working-point, and mechanism observations tied to the best-control trajectory. Agreement would support H1 within the replayed conditions; disagreement would weaken it and support H2, while also requiring separation of model mismatch, temporal sampling, initialization, and control-parameter coupling. Until such evidence exists, continuous-time compliance, robustness, repeatability, hardware performance, equilibrium validity, and global nonlinear feasibility or infeasibility remain unresolved.
